title: RL-Trader: Generalization and Evaluation Rigor in Deep Reinforcement Learning
description:
Deep reinforcement learning is unusually easy to fool yourself with: agents memorize their training trajectory, and a single lucky random seed can masquerade as a real result. This work studies both failure modes from scratch — a PyTorch implementation of Proximal Policy Optimization (PPO), two custom Gymnasium environments, and a full evaluation suite — using financial markets as a deliberately hard testbed: non-stationary, partially observable, with a noisy reward and near–random-walk signal.

The headline result is negative, and that is the point: on real markets the agent has no seed-robust edge over buy-and-hold, and the project's own significance tooling catches a single-seed “+275%” run as a false positive. The work introduces a surrogate-data falsification test that separates “the agent is weak” from “there is no signal to find,” validated with a positive control on synthetic data with known structure.

In doing so it reproduces, in a new domain, the central methodological finding of Henderson et al. (2018) — that single-run RL evaluation is unreliable — and then applies that finding to its own ablation, reporting both arms as distributions over five seeds where all four confidence intervals exclude zero.
notes: Source, figures, and the full evaluation suite are in the linked repository. All reported results are reproducible with the seeds and commands documented in the README.
